name: Ainalrami
description: A star 345 parsecs away, 80 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92761: radius 80.369 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 2009.96 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.119) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92761: effective temperature 4314 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.081)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 0.92 from 2014AJ....147..137L; the 2 published values span log g 0.92 to 0.92, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92761: distance 344.828 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.103), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 345 parsecs away, 80 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 2,010 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,314 K, so 80.369 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 92761: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Nu1 Sagittarii
quotes.card: Nu1 Sagittarii (ν1 Sagittarii, abbreviated Nu1 Sgr, ν1 Sgr) is a triple star system about 1,100 light-years from Earth.
quotes.introduction: The two resolved components are designated Nu1 Sagittarii A (officially named Ainalrami, the traditional name for the system), and B. Component A is itself a spectroscopic binary.
